speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis.

The clinical presentation of subacute motor weakness, gait instability, and cognitive/psychiatric changes (forgetfulness, paranoia) in a 44-year-old male is highly suggestive of Multiple Sclerosis. I will now request MRI images of the brain and spine to visualize potential demyelinating lesions.
